memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: They rose greatly on the earth, and all the high mountains under the entire heavens were covered... Every living thing that moved on land perished - birds, livestock, wild animals, all the creatures that swarm over the earth, and all mankind. - Gen 7:19-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a hard passage, and we should not rush past it or soften it. The judgement was vast and complete - the waters covered the mountains, and every living thing outside the ark perished. Scripture does not flinch from telling us the terrible reach of God's judgement on sin. It is sobering, and it is meant to be.

We live in a time that likes to imagine God will never really judge sin, that His love means He simply overlooks everything. But the flood stands as a solemn witness that God is holy and that sin is deadly serious. He is patient - He gave that world a hundred and twenty years - but His patience is not endless, and sin's wages are real.

We must let this truth do its sobering work in us. Sin is not a small thing. It grieves God, corrupts the world, and brings judgement. To treat it lightly is to misunderstand both God's holiness and our danger.

Yet even this dark passage drives us to the gospel. The New Testament tells us the flood points forward to a final judgement (2 Pet 3:5-7), but also that God provides an ark of safety. The same seriousness of sin that brought the flood is what took Jesus to the cross. He bore the judgement we deserved, so that all who are "in Him" pass safely through. The flood shows us why we so desperately need a Saviour.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you take the seriousness of sin as seriously as God does?
- Have you fled to the only safe refuge from judgement, Jesus Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, help me never to treat sin lightly, for You are holy and sin is deadly. Thank You that Jesus bore the judgement I deserved. Keep me safe in Him, my only refuge.
